sphere_commentary.overview:
Across 1000 outcome observations spanning 30 protocols, the library shows moderately high efficacy with meaningful heterogeneity across series and entry states.
• HEALING leads in listener consistency and raw mean (6.98), reflecting its nervous-system regulation focus and design maturity
• THRIVING (mean 6.96) peaks in Focus & Clarity, with T-FC-L3 crossing into strong-confidence territory at 7.63
• TRANSFORMING carries the lowest mean (6.59) and widest spread, consistent with its ascending-arc intent for low-affect states
• YouTube reach is uniformly thin (max 30 views, no retention data), so efficacy cannot yet be cleanly separated from discovery
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series-level patterns align with design intent but mask meaningful within-series variation that warrants finer-grained reading.
• HEALING holds the highest mean and tightest spread; anxiety and over-stimulation entries perform above the series average while crisis entries sit lower — structurally expected
• THRIVING shows moderate spread with a clear gradient — Focus & Clarity outperforms Creative Flow and Maintenance & Balance, suggesting HOLD arcs serve attentional goals more cleanly than generative ones
• TRANSFORMING carries the highest variance, with ASCENT protocols showing wider distributions than DESCENT — X-MD-L1 and X-MD-L2 both fall below the 50% positive threshold
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols deviate from their series-level expectations in ways that the panel flagged consistently.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean 5.70, std 2.45) sits far below TRANSFORMING mean with high variance — possible subgroup split or design-target mismatch given early sample
• X-MD-L1 (n=22, pct_pos 45%) and X-MD-L2 (n=14, pct_pos 43%) both fall below the 50% positive threshold — ASCENT for motivation appears structurally weaker
• AutoGluon predicts motivation zone score 7.876 for X-MD-L1 versus observed 6.36 — meaningful model–observation tension worth investigating
• Cross-run embedding drift is widespread — 28 of 30 protocols show similarity below 0.85, with X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), and X-ME-L2 (0.532) showing the largest shifts
• H-CR-L1 (mean 6.35) is the lowest HEALING mean — structurally expected for crisis arrival but worth tracking whether lower scores reflect protocol design or entry-state severity
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Concrete protocol actions follow from the patterns above, prioritised by panel convergence.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MD-L1 (n=22, mean 6.36, pct_pos 45%) — extend hold phase or add brief descent at outset to improve motivation entry-state grounding before ASCENT
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean 5.70, std 2.45) — investigate population split and consider whether target audience or design intent needs revision before further recruitment
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC-L3 (n=35, mean 7.63, pct_pos 71%) — scale to additional zones where focus is a secondary goal and expand YouTube reach given highest THRIVING views (15)
• X-MD-L2 (n=14, mean 6.21) — too early for redesign; track whether low scores reflect ASCENT arc design or adviser routing mismatch
• H-SL-L1 (n=54, strong confidence, drift 0.530) — re-examine analytical framing given the strong outcome scores alongside high cross-run drift
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Embedding context is available but tells a consistent story of analytical instability rather than protocol-level divergence, and clustering is currently undersupported.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: widespread drift across 28 of 30 protocols — X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), and X-ME-L2 (0.532) lead the shift; only H-OS-L1 (0.821) and X-ME-L1 (0.818) remain relatively stable
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: insufficient data — too few embeddings accumulated to support meaningful clustering at this time
• Confidence note: drift values derive from only two historical runs per protocol, so interpretations should remain tentative until more accumulated history anchors the baseline

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Listeners report strong relief from anxiety and stress, with most settling within ten minutes and describing the rhythm as grounding. A robust, well-evidenced protocol that reliably helps listeners arrive at calm.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: A gentler variant that still helps with anxiety, though some listeners take a little longer to settle. Most describe it as comfortable and calming, with a slightly more reserved overall response than Meadow.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: The deepest of the anxiety protocols, often described as very settling and calming once listeners give it time. The pace asks for patience but rewards it with a noticeable sense of release.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Designed for moments of acute distress, this protocol meets listeners where they are and helps them stabilise — most report significant improvement even in difficult states. The lower average score reflects how hard it is to arrive already overwhelmed.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: A crisis protocol that supports listeners through acute distress with a strong settling response. Average scores are lower than other HEALING protocols because the entry state is harder, not because the protocol underperforms.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: The quickest to settle of the crisis protocols — many listeners find calm within the first minute or two. Some find the music takes a moment to warm to, but the rhythm consistently delivers.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: A reliable anchor for overstimulated nervous systems — listeners describe feeling grounded, with music they love and rhythm that holds them steady. The most-used over-stimulation protocol in the library.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: A softer over-stimulation protocol that takes a little more time to land but offers a gentle, calming experience. Listeners often describe it as rainfall for the senses.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: A glacial-paced variant that many listeners use before sleep — the slower arc gives the nervous system space to settle without abruptness.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: A strong sleep protocol that helps most listeners settle quickly and drift off with ease. The music is widely liked and the rhythm reads as comforting rather than busy.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: A hammock-paced sleep protocol that takes a bit longer to settle in, but most listeners find the gentler arc easier to surrender to.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: A midnight-arc sleep protocol with a slightly busier opening — some listeners love the momentum, others prefer the slower L1 and L2 variants.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: A steady creative-flow protocol that helps listeners find their groove, with a balanced feel that suits most people.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: A tighter, more focused creative-flow variant that listeners describe as helping them enter flow state more easily.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: The deepest creative-flow protocol — listeners report noticeable and significant improvement, though the longer arc takes patience.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: A focus protocol with a slightly busier opening that some listeners find energising and others find too active.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: A gentler focus protocol that settles more gradually and helps listeners arrive at clarity without rushing.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: The strongest focus protocol in the library — listeners report significant improvement, sustained clarity, and balanced energy.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: A grounding maintenance protocol with a long settle arc that rewards patience — most listeners feel more centred by the end.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: A more varied maintenance protocol with a wider response range — some listeners find it slightly busier than they expected.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: A high-positive maintenance protocol that lands well for many listeners, though a small group reports not settling.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: A mind-and-clarity protocol that helps most listeners feel clearer, with a few reporting it made things worse — worth approaching gently.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: A settling mind-and-clarity protocol with strong rhythm appeal and quick arrival at calm.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Early data and high variability make this the most uncertain protocol in the library — some listeners respond well, others do not.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: A motivation protocol that works for many listeners but not all — the data suggests the ASCENT arc may benefit from more grounding at the start.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: An early-data motivation protocol with a longer settle arc and modest outcomes — worth watching as more responses come in.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: A promising motivation protocol with the highest mean in its entry despite high variability — early signal suggests it may resonate with a specific listener subgroup.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: A widely-loved mood-and-energy protocol that listeners describe as uplifting, with music that consistently lands.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: A sunrise-paced mood-and-energy protocol that helps listeners feel significant improvement, particularly when given time to settle.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: A mood-and-energy ASCENT with mixed results — many listeners report noticeable improvement, but a notable minority report no effect.
